questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to the side to clear the path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the side to clear the path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, you must slow down, make room for the emergency vehicle, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the labels before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive anyway, even if labels warn against it.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability. Check the label for warnings about driving. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Rain reduces visibility, so you must slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Use your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and stay at a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and stay at a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without sudden braking. This protects you from drivers behind you who may crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or horns and flashing red or blue lights. Follow instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles may follow each other, so only proceed when you are certain it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes wrong.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, changes your judgment of speed and distance, reduces recovery from headlight glare, and often makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not needed if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder toward the next lane before changing lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and be ready to stop?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is a possible penalty for a first driving under the influence conviction?

options.text: Three years in state prison and a $3,000 fine
Three months in county jail
Two months in county jail and a $30 fine
Six months in county jail and a $1,000 fine

questions.correctAnswerText: Six months in county jail and a $1,000 fine
questions.explanation: A first DUI conviction can result in fines up to $1,000, jail time up to six months, and license suspension for up to 45 days, depending on your age and blood alcohol level. Penalties are higher if a child is endangered, someone is injured, or someone dies.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them too. High beams bounce off fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Regardless of your direction.
Only if it is following you.
Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regardless of your direction.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether it is coming from behind you or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time allows a person to recover from alcohol's effects.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look into the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers are more likely to find you if you stay with your vehicle. Leaving your car in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.
Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have gates or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
You must slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you have a clear view of approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you have a clear view of approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve.
Turn right or left.
You can only drive in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign tells you that all traffic must go in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It gets larger.
It gets smaller.
It is easier to see cross traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets smaller.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. When you drive faster, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe speed for driving?

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe for traffic conditions.
A speed that is safe for current road and weather conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must follow the speed limit and drive at a speed that is safe for the area, traffic, weather, road quality, and light. Adjust your speed to conditions around you.

questions.question: What is a danger of driving much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: You are a very safe driver.
You always have the right-of-way.
Other cars should not pass you.
You may create a dangerous situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may create a dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is hazardous. If cars back up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.
